This page is the readable version of the
[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/tpogden/clerq/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md), which
has the full list of changes. Versions are newest first, and
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) applies: a minor version adds
features, and anything marked **breaking** will need a change to your code or
a recalculation of your results.

Entries before 0.13.0 use the old package name, `maxwellbloch`, and its old
class names, as they were at the time. See
[MaxwellBloch is now clerq](news/rename.qmd) for the rename.

## 0.15.0 — 24 October 2026

**Float32 gradients.** `clerq.autodiff` no longer insists on 64-bit precision. It computes in
whatever precision JAX is set to, so it runs with JAX's default (float32) as well as with
`jax_enable_x64`, and the solver tolerances default to values each precision can meet. On the
benchmark problems float32 agrees with float64 to $10^{-6}$ to $2\times10^{-5}$ in the field and $6\times10^{-7}$ to
$5\times10^{-5}$ in gradients, and runs 1.1 to 2.1 times faster on the CPU. Keep float64 for finite-difference checks and when you need
tight tolerances. See [Autodiff performance and validation](usage/autodiff-performance.qmd).

**Doppler class spacing.** `velocity_classes` takes a new `thermal_delta_spacing`, a
maximum spacing between the classes, in place of `thermal_delta_steps`. Pass `"auto"` for the
largest spacing with no spurious Doppler echo: a grid of spacing $h$ repeats the response of a
Doppler-dependent coherence at $t = 1/(b h)$, and the result is wrong if that falls inside the
time window and is not damped by the decay. `"auto"` uses each level's Doppler shift and the
decay rates, so it depends on the system as well as the window; `thermal_delta_echo_tolerance`
sets how far the echo must be damped, and the spacing is also kept fine enough to resolve the thermal width. See [Velocity Classes](usage/velocity-classes.ipynb).

**Velocity-class weights (changes results).** Each class is now weighted by the detuning
interval it represents as well as its Boltzmann density. Before, a non-uniform grid (an inner
band from `thermal_delta_inner_*`) over-weighted the densely sampled region, so such results
change. Uniform grids are unchanged. `thermal_weights` is still the density; the intervals are
`thermal_widths` and the weights used are `thermal_quadrature_weights`. A savefile solved before
this on a non-uniform grid is rejected on load: delete it or pass `recalc=True`.

## 0.14.0 — 23 October 2026

**Unit conversions.** The new `clerq.macro` module converts laboratory quantities
(intensity, beam power, temperature, density, linewidth) to clerq's MHz, µs and cm units. See
[Converting from Experimental Units](usage/units.ipynb).

**DC magnetic field.** A system can now sit in a static B-field along the
quantisation axis: add a `b_field` block (magnitude, units, and the per-level
`g_F` and `m_F`) and each sublevel shifts by $g_F m_F \mu_B B$. For hyperfine
atoms `Atom1e.get_zeeman_levels()` supplies `g_F` and `m_F`, and the field can be a
differentiable parameter of `to_autodiff()`. See the
[B-field usage page](usage/b-field.ipynb). Without a `b_field` nothing changes.

**Stability checks.** `solve()` now stops with `PropagationInstabilityError` when
the field blows up, and warns when the z-step looks too coarse (estimated from
the difference between the Euler and Adams-Bashforth predictions, available as
`solver.step_error_estimate`). Pass `z_steps_inner="auto"` to refine the step
automatically, or `check_stability=False` to switch the checks off. See
[Numerical Stability and Step Sizes](usage/numerical-stability.ipynb).

**Time-grid checks.** `solve()` also warns when `t_steps` is too coarse to
resolve the fields and coherences, or when the time window cuts off a pulse or
its ringing, and `suggest_t_steps()` estimates a grid from the problem's
frequency scales before you solve.

**Gradients through the propagation (optional, experimental).** With
`pip install 'clerq[jax]'`, `solver.to_autodiff()` returns a differentiable
version of a `PropagationSolver` problem: exact gradients of any loss of the
propagated field with respect to pulse parameters, interaction strengths,
detunings, decay rates or a sampled input field, for about the cost of five to six
propagations however many parameters there are. It is meant for gradient-based
design of pulses and media, and `ad.minimize(loss, params)` follows the gradient
with an optax optimiser (Adam by default). `import clerq` itself never loads JAX. See the
[pulse design example](examples/autodiff-pulse-design.ipynb) and the
[API reference](api/autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.qmd), and `CHANGELOG.md` for the
supported features and limits.

Each decay's `rate` is a parameter too (`decay_rates`, for spontaneous decay, ground-state
decoherence or dephasing), and `clerq.autodiff.controls` expands a free-form control in a few
smooth functions, which stops an optimiser from exploiting the time grid.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Detuned fields: results change
Earlier versions drove the Hamiltonian with the real part of the field only. That is
exact for resonant, real fields on a symmetric, equally weighted velocity-class grid
(those results are unchanged), but wrong for a single detuned field, a two-photon
offset or an asymmetric class grid: a weak probe through an optical depth of 6 at two
half-widths detuning came out with transmission 1.1 (unphysical) instead of 0.30.
`PropagationSolver` and `to_autodiff()` now use the full complex envelope. Rerun any
detuned results from older versions. `PropagationSolver(real_drive=True)` reproduces
the old behaviour and is deprecated.
:::

**Cyclic field accessor.** `solver.rabi_freqs_zt` is the solved field as a cyclic
Rabi frequency, the same unit as `rabi_freq` in the problem definition, so you no
longer divide by $2\pi$. `solver.Omegas_zt` (angular) is deprecated but still works,
and the arrays returned by `solve()` are unchanged. The output of `to_autodiff()`
is cyclic too, so it compares directly with `rabi_freqs_zt`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Upgrading from 0.13.1
Your code keeps working: the old names still run and raise a
`DeprecationWarning`. Switching to the new names now will save you work when
they are removed in a future release.
:::

**Clearer names, all available from `import clerq`.**

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `clerq.mb_solve.MBSolve` | `clerq.PropagationSolver` |
| `clerq.ob_solve.OBSolve` | `clerq.LindbladSolver` |
| `clerq.ob_atom.OBAtom` | `clerq.System` |
| `clerq.field.Field` | `clerq.Field` |
| `mbsolve()`, `obsolve()` | `solve()` |
| `atom` (argument, attribute, JSON key) | `system` |

- "System" replaces "atom" because the solvers work for any few-level open
  quantum system, not only atoms.
- The modules are now `clerq.propagation`, `clerq.lindblad`, `clerq.system`
  and `clerq.system_base`.
- Helper functions that take a solver always call that argument `solver`.
  Before, it was `mb_solve` in `spectral`, `fixed` and `fileio`, and `mbs` in
  `plot`.
- `mbsolve_euler()` and `mbsolve_ab()` are deprecated in favour of
  `solve(step=...)`.
- The `mbsolve` and `obsolve` command-line scripts keep their names.

**Fixed: solving twice gave different results.** Calling `solver.solve()` again on
the same `PropagationSolver` (or editing a field's `rabi_freq_t_args` and
solving again) started from the last solve's leftover field instead of the
pulse you defined, so the second and later results were wrong. Repeated solves
now match a fresh solver. If you re-solved the same object, recalculate.

**Fixed: Adams-Bashforth output was one inner step early.** With the default
`step="ab"` and `z_steps_inner > 1` (the default is 2), each stored slice of
the field and the states was one inner step short of its nominal `z`. Slices are
now at `zlist[j]`. Problems with `z_steps_inner=1`, and `step="euler"`, are
unchanged, and so are problems whose medium starts a couple of inner steps
after `z_min`, because a second error cancelled the first there. Problems
where the medium reaches `z_min` (for example `z_min=0` with the medium from
`z=0`) shift, by an amount first order in the inner step: re-run them and
discard old `.qu` files. This is a correction; there is nothing to change in
your code.

**Cached results.** A `.qu` savefile made by an earlier version no longer
matches its problem definition (which now has a `system` key), so it is solved
again and overwritten the first time you use it.

**Other changes**

- `PropagationSolver` and `System` have class docstrings describing their
  arguments.
- The release assets on GitHub are now just the wheel, the sdist and their
  attestations.
- The documentation has correct API page titles, and several docstrings that
  disagreed with their signatures are fixed.
- The lockfile is updated to clear security alerts in documentation and
  development packages. The installed package is unaffected.

## 0.13.1 — 9 October 2026

A fix-up release after the rename.

**Fixed**

- The `mbsolve` and `obsolve` command-line scripts work again. They had been
  broken since 0.10.0 and 0.11.0, and `mbsolve` also failed on Python 3.14. The
  unused `--pbarchunksize` option is removed.
- The example notebooks are recalibrated after the 0.13.0 factor-of-2 fix, so
  each example solves the physical problem it was designed for and gives the
  same results as in 0.12.0.

**Added**

- The stimulated three-pulse photon echo example.
- `CITATION.cff`, so GitHub's "Cite this repository" works.

**Changed**

- clerq is described as classical Maxwell fields propagating through open
  quantum systems, not as a Maxwell–Bloch solver.
- The documentation outputs are regenerated cleanly, and there is a page
  explaining the new name.

## 0.13.0 — 9 October 2026

::: {.callout-important}
## Breaking: results change
The Maxwell propagation equation was missing a factor of 2, so the optical
depth in earlier versions was **half** its physical value. Absorption and
propagation results change, so recompute any cached `.qu` results and any
figures made with earlier versions. The theory curves in `clerq.spectral` are
updated to match.
:::

- **Renamed from `maxwellbloch` to `clerq`.** Change `import maxwellbloch` to
  `import clerq`. The PyPI name is also `clerq`, the Plotly theme is named
  `"clerq"`, and `.qu` files record the `clerq` version.
- The documentation moved from Sphinx and Read the Docs to Quarto, at
  [clerq.org](https://clerq.org).

## 0.12.0 — 6 May 2026

- **Plotting:** `plot.field_profile` and `plot.field_z_profile_anim`, a
  `show_z_bounds` option, and a `speed_of_light` option to plot in the fixed
  frame. `plot.spectrum` accepts x-axis bounds.
- **Faster:** the number-density profile is computed once up front, and the
  inner loop over sigma operators is vectorised.
- **Examples:** the SIT, linear absorption, V-system and Λ EIT/slow-light
  examples are each merged into one notebook.

## 0.11.0 — 3 May 2026

**New**

- **Counter-propagating fields:** `Field(counter_propagating=True)` models a
  field travelling against the others. If the field has depleted so much that
  forward-only propagation is no longer valid, a
  `CounterPropagatingDepletionError` is raised (turn the check off with
  `check_counter_prop_depletion=False`).
- **Plotting module** `plot`, built on Plotly with a shared theme: field
  space-time and envelope plots, spectra, populations, coherences and pulse
  area. Install it with the `plot` extra.
- **Spectral windows:** the FFT functions in `spectral` accept a SciPy
  `window`, and `plot.spectrum` gains `freq_range`, an `arcsinh` frequency
  scale and `window`.
- **New examples:** Autler–Townes splitting, CPT dark resonance, adiabatons,
  two-pulse photon echo, odd-π sech pulses and the Rb 87 D2 cycling
  transition, plus an examples gallery page.

**Breaking**

- The printed progress reports of `MBSolve.mbsolve` and its `pbar_chunk_size`
  argument are replaced by a tqdm progress bar. Use `progress` (default
  `True`) and `progress_show_area` to control it, and remove any
  `pbar_chunk_size` argument.

## 0.10.0 — 25 April 2026

**Breaking**

- `OBSolve.solve` is renamed `OBSolve.obsolve`.

**New**

- **Savefile check:** a `.qu` file stores a hash of its problem definition and
  the library versions. Loading a file built from a different problem raises
  `ValueError`, and older files load with a warning.
- Generated API reference pages.

**Fixed**

- A missing savefile directory is created before the `.qu` file is written.
- An `IndexError` when fields are added to a system after construction.

**Changed**

- `maxwell_boltzmann` moved to `utility` and gained an `offset` parameter.

## 0.9.0 — 24 April 2026

- **About 43× faster** inner propagation loop, from building the field
  interpolation once per z-step with QuTiP 5.
- `Field.upper_levels()` and `Field.lower_levels()` return the sorted level
  indices a field couples.
- `LevelF` checks that `|J−I| ≤ F ≤ J+I` and raises `ValueError` for
  impossible hyperfine quantum numbers.
- Internal methods are renamed with a leading `_` to mark them as private
  (for example `build_H_0` is now `_build_H_0`). If you called any of these
  directly, update the name.

## 0.8.1 — 23 April 2026

Maintenance: type annotations throughout, mutable default arguments fixed,
more tests, and a docs build in CI. `fixed.rabi_freq_abs` is removed; use
`fixed.rabi_freq(..., part="abs")`.

## 0.8.0 — 15 April 2026

A modernisation release.

- Supports QuTiP 5, NumPy 2 and SciPy 1.14+.
- **Python 3.10 or later is required.**
- Packaging moved to `pyproject.toml`; uv is the main environment manager.
- CI moved to GitHub Actions with trusted publishing to PyPI.
